change_note: Batch 7: index-fund tracking and fees, two-front selloffs and AI free cash flow, synchronized chip setups.

items.text: About 20% of S&P 500 members were above their 50-day average, the zone that preceded several rebounds since 2020.
Fear and Greed index read 28 (fear). The S&P 500 printed a doji on 1 Oct and sat about 2% below its all-time high.
Nike fell about 5.7% after earnings: profit beat, but weak forward guidance.
Accenture rose about 15% and Micron about 3% after profit beats.
Alphabet slipped about 1.7% and was described as still inside a technical triangle.
Synopsys reportedly signed a chip development agreement with OpenAI.
Rocket Lab reportedly won a 20-launch contract but was meeting resistance at its 150-day average.
Nu Holdings denied rumours that it would acquire a UK digital bank.
Energy rose about 2% on geopolitical tension around the Strait of Hormuz.
Meta's shopping agent was reported at the top of the App Store, with Amazon said to be blocking it. Amazon ad revenue cited at about 68.6B dollars a year.
Cited Morgan Stanley figures: about 5% of purchases made by AI agents, 42% of users using AI to help them shop, and a 20% chance agents dominate online retail by 2030.
Named as likely winners of the agent era: Meta, card networks, Shopify, Walmart, PayPal and compute or chip suppliers.
Named as at risk in the agent era: travel aggregators, subscription gyms, news subscriptions and telecoms.
Six unrelated growth names were described as tracing the same chart pattern into earnings.
AMD and Arm shared a pattern: consolidation, breakout around 1 Apr, then a steep climb. AMD was cited up about 83% since then.

Palantir: implied move about 11%, revenue estimate about 1B dollars (+73% YoY), EPS estimate 0.29. The commercial vs government mix was the key line. A large short by a well-known investor was reported.
PayPal: implied move about 9.5% after a 31% bounce from February lows. Transaction revenue was cited up about 4% and Venmo about 20%. A turnaround under the new CEO was the test.
AMD: revenue growth estimate about 30%. It had to show AI inference demand in data center and client to justify the premium.
Uber had broken its downtrend line and retested support. A strong EPS beat and guidance were needed to confirm the reversal.
Arm: implied move about 14%, revenue estimate +18%. It had broken out of a long 80 to 190 dollar range, with a technical target near 280.
AppLovin had dropped about 19% the prior quarter, was forming a possible head-and-shoulders, and needed to clear resistance near 525.
IonQ: loss-making. The market wanted deployment numbers and updates on a reported 9.7B dollar data-center partnership with Microsoft.
About 180 S&P 500 companies (36% of the index) were reporting in one week alongside a Fed rate decision.
Robinhood: implied move about 10.6%, revenue above 1B dollars. Crypto vs fiat volumes, net interest revenue and prediction markets were the lines to watch.
SoFi: implied move about 11.8%, revenue estimate 1.04 to 1.05B dollars, down about 30% YTD with resistance near 19. Galileo platform growth was the doubted segment.
Alphabet: implied move about 5.9%, revenue estimate about 91B dollars (+20% YoY), EPS 2.63. Cloud growth, YouTube ads and capex mix (own chips vs Nvidia) were key.
Microsoft: implied move about 7%, revenue estimate about 81B dollars, chart weak vs peers. Azure growth, paid Copilot adoption and OpenAI terms were the swing factors.
Meta: implied move about 8%, revenue estimate about 55B dollars, EPS 6.71. A workforce cut was rumoured; capex guidance, Llama traction and Reality Labs burn were key.
Amazon: implied move about 6%, revenue estimate about 177B dollars, near all-time highs. AWS growth was the driver; retail margins were secondary.
Apple: implied move about 3%, revenue estimate about 109B dollars. Only an on-device AI timeline or news on a reported CEO transition was expected to move it.
Fear and Greed read 35 (fear) while the S&P 500 was two days from its all-time high.
The 10-year Treasury yield was cited at 5.11%, driven by weak PMI data, hawkish Fed signals, a poor 5-year auction and crude near 92 dollars.
Inflation was described as driven by business inputs, chiefly memory and semiconductor pricing (for example TSMC price increases), rather than housing or retail.
Alphabet broke below its 150-day average. A thin-volume zone below 345 put 319 to 321 in play unless 345 was reclaimed.
Palantir broke above 188 on rising volume after a base that followed a fall from 207 to 106. Next target cited near 271; 187 had to hold as support.
Amazon launched an AI seller-assistance plugin, read as a push back against Meta's shopping agent.
Cited via Charlie Bilello: 57 all-time highs in 2024, 27 in 2026 to mid-August, and more than 1,400 since 1929, about one trading day in ten.
The semiconductor index was cited about 18% below its peak, with a warning that euphoric chip runs often end in 30 to 50% corrections.
Bank of America defended Nvidia: forward P/E about 20 vs 21.3 for the S&P 500, trailing 31 vs 28. About 1T dollars of value was off the peak.
Nvidia tested its 150-day average three times and broke its descending line from the 232 and 213 peaks, with near-term resistance at 212.
Bitcoin miners pivoting to host AI compute (neo-cloud) were drawing new volume and buyers.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 had moved sideways at the same levels since mid-May, waiting on mega-cap earnings.
Apple broke above 288.62 on rising volume, under 10 dollars from its high, making higher highs and lows.
Amazon had traded sideways since December 2024. A breakout needed a move above 250, and the 150-day average near 234 had to hold.
Alphabet was 12% off its highs but held support at 349 on its 150-day average, keeping the uptrend.
Meta broke its uptrend on 1 Aug 2025 and sat in a falling channel on its 150-week average. It needed to clear 740 to reverse.
Microsoft was about 30% off its highs. Support was cited at 344.70, and it needed to clear 466 for a higher high.
Nvidia corrected from 236 to 194 and sat on long-term rising support and its 150-day average near 192. Holding 185 to 192 kept the bullish structure.
Tesla was described as flat since October 2021 despite wild swings, resting on long-term rising support near 372.
Weekly: Nasdaq +6.5%, S&P 500 +4.5% to 7,126 (about +12% in 11 days). Software ETF +13.9%, led by Oracle +26%.
Rally drivers cited: ceasefire hopes, calmer Strait of Hormuz with oil down 7% to 92 dollars, strong bank earnings and a tame PPI print.
Retail chatter focused on Nvidia, Tesla robotaxi, Microsoft, Netflix, an Allbirds pivot, space and quantum names, and squeeze talk in Opendoor and GameStop.
S&P 500 stretched above its 20- and 50-day averages with two or three unfilled gaps below. A pullback toward 7,000 was expected; Fear and Greed read greed.

Israeli housing: banks were described as heavily funding developers with unsold inventory, who avoid official price cuts. Ministry of Finance data was cited to show buyers hold unusual negotiating power.
13F data was cited showing large institutions cut their Micron holdings by about 92%, rotating into other tech and semiconductor names (destinations not given in the batch).
Nvidia was described as trading at a lower forward P/E than the S&P 500, because earnings growth had outrun the share price.
2026 outlooks reviewed: Evercore expected a K-shaped recovery led by four sectors. Jefferies highlighted internet, software, biotech and quantum computing.
Israeli pension and provident S&P 500 tracks were cited returning anywhere from 4.2% to 8.5% over the same period, because loose rules let funds imitate rather than hold the index.

Suggested targets: management fees of 0.1% to 0.2% of accumulated savings, plus transparency on USD/ILS conversion. The Selis case, with losses in unregulated alternative assets, was cited against Israel's IRA model.
Broad selloff: Russell -0.6%, S&P 500 -1.2%, Nasdaq -1.8%. Oil up 36% to 91 dollars on Hormuz tension; 10-year yield 4.69%, highest since Jan 2025. VIX briefly topped 20 and was sold.
Alphabet fell about 7% after earnings: strong revenue, but its first negative free cash flow since 2015 because of AI capex.
Intel beat on revenue and EPS and rose more than 4% after hours.
The KOSPI broke out of a bull flag. Being chip-heavy (Samsung, SK Hynix), it was read as a lead for semiconductors once geopolitical fear eases.
Semiconductors shared one setup: a steep rally, a sharp drop, and an attempt to break the falling resistance line.
The software ETF was coiling in a symmetrical triangle (possible cup and handle) and needed a confirmed break above 104.
Nvidia was breaking its falling resistance line but was stretched above its 150- and 200-day averages.
A well-known investor disclosed new shorts in Oracle and Nebius; Nebius fell 13%, though it was already far above its 150-day average.
The S&P 500 was stretched near its upper bounds, waiting on the jobs report and the Jackson Hole symposium.
